plan.method: Diagnostic cross-format comparison, 3 fixed repetitions in rotated/reversed order, not a 5-percent regression qualification. Same bytes, same 16 MiB durable epochs; native CRC32, HDF5 none/Fletcher32, SQLite FULL WAL, raw lower bound; semantics differ. All bytes validated by identical Rust function; no compression. Cached reads, not cold-device throughput. Separate process/phase CPU; process RSS and IO from native-child wait4. No concurrent builds or observers during timings.

corrected_sqlite_plan.replaces: All original SQLite timing observations, including successful ones; those attempts remain retained.

interpretation.practicality: Report absolute stage time and throughput; a multiple against raw alone is insufficient to call a rich format impractical. Compare 100,000,000 samples/s at 16/32/64 bits = 190.73486328125 / 381.4697265625 / 762.939453125 MiB/s. These are conditional payload rates, not a claim of a measured end-to-end acquisition pipeline.
interpretation.normal: 64 KiB,1 MiB,4 MiB grouped payloads; tiny 128-byte and 4-KiB diagnostic rows are separate.
interpretation.reader_scope: Eight threads each open and fully scan a stable committed file. Parallel phase includes open; no concurrent ingestion in this cross-format harness. Prior varlit-only concurrent-writer results remain separate.
interpretation.limits: Cached Linux filesystem, uncompressed data, three repetitions; not cold-storage or all-platform qualification. CRC32 and Fletcher32 are different checksum contracts; SQLite FULL WAL and HDF5 fsync do not have identical crash-recovery semantics.
